- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early forecast periods (first 5–10 days of the 30-day window).
- Forecasts peak too early and then gradually decline, while true outcomes often show sharper, delayed peaks or sudden drops.
- After a spike in true values (e.g., 74–76), model fails to adjust downward quickly — overestimates remain inflated for several days.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: forecasts trend downward too slowly, failing to reflect rapid true price corrections.
- Forecasts lag behind true outcomes by 1–3 days in the early part of the window, then catch up or overshoot.
- Overshoot after spikes: model forecasts peak higher than true peak, then slowly decay, while true values drop more abruptly.
- Model underestimates low-range true values (e.g., 67–68) and fails to anticipate sharp downward corrections.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts are overly optimistic in the first 10 days, then become more accurate later — suggesting model needs dynamic weighting or adaptive horizon calibration.
